sources.title: Human History Map historical-basemap civilization index
sources.note: Exact repository row checked: id shaskanka is labeled Shaskanka, marked circa and historical-basemaps generated, indexed 600 to 700, and has neither aliases nor an authored link.

sources.title: Human History Map research coverage ledger
sources.note: Coverage record checked for kind state, one border file, observed interval 600 to 700, missing card and review, approximate dates and unreviewed identity, chronology and border fields.

sources.title: Human History Map world-500 topology
sources.note: Decoded predecessor seam: the exact id is absent and the broad imported Gupta Empire feature owns all twenty audited points from Bengal and Bihar through coastal Odisha.

sources.title: Human History Map world-600 topology
sources.note: Decoded exact target layer, raw arcs, geometry statistics, coordinate hash, shared-arc neighbors and point ownership for twenty named places across Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, Kanauj and Kamarupa.

sources.title: Human History Map world-700 topology
sources.note: Decoded endpoint seam: shaskanka disappears and a Pala polygon immediately takes most audited eastern points, a transition several decades earlier than the accepted rise of Gopala.

sources.title: Human History Map world-800 topology
sources.note: Decoded later comparison seam: the Pala feature remains across most audited eastern points, while western and southern points fall under other imported ids.

sources.title: Shashanka, Banglapedia
sources.note: National encyclopedia biography checked for chronology, Karnasuvarna, inscriptions and coins, political expansion, rivalry with Harsha and Bhaskaravarman, source problems and the coexistence of flourishing Buddhist institutions.

sources.title: Karnasuvarna, Banglapedia
sources.note: National encyclopedia entry checked for the capital's identification near Rajbadidanga, Xuanzang's description, Bhaskaravarman's post-Shashanka victory camp and Jayanaga's later rule from Karnasuvarna.

sources.title: Raktamrttika Mahavihara, Banglapedia
sources.note: Entry checked for Xuanzang's learned monks, Rajbadidanga excavations, monastery plan, sealings, fifth-to-eighth-century dating and the archaeological identification of Karnasuvarna nearby.

sources.title: Political Geography, Banglapedia
sources.note: Regional synthesis checked for post-Gupta political geography, changing divisions of Bengal, the interval after Shashanka and the traditional placement of Gopala's election in the mid-eighth century.

sources.title: Egra Copper Plate Inscription, Museums of India
sources.note: Indian Museum object record checked for copper, dimensions, provenance, seventh-century dating, Shashanka attribution, twenty obverse and seventeen reverse lines and probable land-grant content.

sources.title: Ganjam plates of Madhavaraja II, Epigraphia Indica volume VI
sources.note: Archaeological Survey publication checked for the Sanskrit charter, Gupta year 300 equivalent to 619 to 20, Shashanka's overlord title, Madhavaraja's subordinate position, solar-eclipse grant and transitional script.

sources.title: Catalogue of Copper Plate Grants, Government Museum Chennai
sources.note: Government museum catalogue checked for the three Ganjam plates, bull seal, Sanskrit, acute-angled transitional script, Kongoda context, learned Brahmin recipient and Gupta year 300 date.

sources.title: Copper, Parchment and Stone: Studies in the Sources for Landholding and Lordship
sources.note: Scholarly source study checked for the Egra-area charter's surveyed boundaries, ditches, markers and water landscape, used to explain how grants turned lived land into written administrative space.

sources.title: Indian Archaeology 1966 to 67: A Review
sources.note: Official Archaeological Survey review checked for Rajbadidanga phases, monastic structures, bowls, dishes, lids, sprinklers, figurines, beads, balls, game objects, nails, metal and shell finds.

sources.title: Indian Archaeology 1962 to 63: A Review
sources.note: Official Archaeological Survey review checked for the first Rajbadidanga campaign, baked-brick walls, mud oven, platforms, possible stupa bases, plastered stairs, beads and sprinkler-shaped vessels.

sources.title: The Archaeological Landscape of Karnasuvarna
sources.note: Peer-reviewed landscape study checked for Bhagirathi flood dynamics, low groundwater, ponds and tanks, ephemeral housing, monastic masonry, granary rice and wheat, cooking vessels and river trade.

sources.title: A Note on Archaeology of Early Medieval Towns in Bengal
sources.note: Scholarly archaeological note checked for the warning that Rajbadidanga is a monastery rather than the whole capital and for merchant sealings as evidence of commerce and patronage.

sources.title: Two Interesting Coins of Sasanka
sources.note: Peer-reviewed numismatic article checked for gold and silver issues and the political setting of Shashanka's rivalry with the Maukharis, Rajyavardhana, Harsha and Bhaskaravarman.

sources.title: Numismatic image dataset for early medieval Gauḍa coinage
sources.note: Open peer-reviewed dataset checked for 262 Gauḍa coin images, four Shashanka classes and recurring Shiva-on-bull, Lakshmi and short legend features; its inconsistent historical dating is not adopted.

sources.title: Catalogue of the Coins of the Gupta Dynasties and of Sasanka
sources.note: British Museum catalogue scan checked for Shashanka coin types, Shiva reclining on Nandi, moon imagery, goddess reverse and the limits of numismatic reconstruction.

sources.title: An Unpublished Gold Coin of Śaśāṅka
sources.note: Asiatic Society article checked for an additional gold type, Shiva and bull design, Brāhmī legend readings including Śaśā and Jaya and comparison with known issues.

sources.title: The Decline of Buddhism in India
sources.note: University study checked for the Bodhi-tree and persecution stories about Shashanka, their source setting and scholarly reasons to avoid turning one hostile narrative into a complete religious policy.

sources.title: Early Epigraphic Notices of Bhāskaravarman
sources.note: Scholarly history scan checked for Bhaskaravarman's alliance with Harsha, rivalry with Shashanka, Xuanzang's visit and the Nidhanpur plates issued from a victory camp at Karnasuvarna.

sources.title: Vappaghosavata Grant of the time of Jayanāga, DHARMA
sources.note: ERC-funded critical digital edition checked for later seventh-century Karnasuvarna, Sanskrit and Northern Brahmi, provincial officers, a Samaveda student, family merit, riverbed and reservoir boundaries.

sources.title: Political Formations in Northern and Eastern India, c. 600 to 750 CE
sources.note: IGNOU university text checked for Shashanka's approximate reign, post-Gupta rise, Gauda-Kanauj-Kamarupa politics, decline after his death and the later emergence of Gopala.

sources.title: Land Grants and Social Change in Early Medieval India
sources.note: IGNOU teaching unit checked for broad regional patterns of land grants, local intermediaries, hierarchy, tax rights and the complexity of applying varna ideals to lived social relations.

sources.title: Status of Women, c. 300 BCE to 800 CE, IGNOU eGyanKosh
sources.note: University course unit checked for broad north Indian evidence about household patriarchy, marriage, widowhood, property, education and work, used only as context because Gauda-specific women's voices are scarce.

sources.title: History of India, 300 to 1200 CE, University of Delhi
sources.note: University history text checked for gendered property limits, stridhana and evidence for women's agricultural and pastoral labor, explicitly treated as broad subcontinental context rather than a Gauda census.

sources.title: Physicians of Ancient India
sources.note: Peer-reviewed history-of-medicine article checked for Vagbhatta, the seventh-century Astangahrdaya and learned Ayurvedic practice, used as contemporary South Asian context rather than proof of a Karnasuvarna clinic.

sources.title: Vāgbhaṭa authority record, National Library of Medicine
sources.note: National Library of Medicine catalogue checked for Vāgbhaṭa's seventh-century floruit and Sanskrit medical authorship, anchoring the medical comparison without inventing local practitioners.

sources.title: Hygiene and health practices in Yijing's Buddhist record
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study checked for Yijing's 671 to 695 Indian travels and prescriptions on washing, tooth sticks, filtered water, clean and dirty water, toilet conduct and the idealized nature of monastic rules.

sources.title: A Record of the Buddhist Religion as Practised in India and the Malay Archipelago
sources.note: IGNCA-hosted translation checked for Yijing's primary descriptions of tooth-wood, washing, water handling and monastic bodily discipline, written after Shashanka and not direct evidence for his palace or households.

sources.title: Bengal and Southeast Asia: Trade and Cultural Contacts in the Ancient Period
sources.note: UNESCO Silk Roads study checked for Bengal's river and maritime networks, Karnasuvarna's capital role and connections through ports and merchant movement.

sources.title: Bengal and Southeast Asian Maritime Contacts: Archaeological Perspectives
sources.note: Peer-reviewed archaeology article checked for material evidence and evidentiary limits in reconstructing Bay of Bengal routes, goods and cultural connections.

proposedOverrides.summary: The atlas's `Shaskanka` is Shashanka of Gauda, whose rule ended by the late 630s although the imported map label lasts to 700.

batchIdentityNotes: Exact target id shaskanka is indexed as Shaskanka, circa 600 to 700, with no aliases or authored link; the historical name is Shashanka or Śaśāṅka and his polity is usually called Gauda.

The only exact layer is one unlabeled 54-position Polygon in world-600 with bounds 83.98343983439833,19.60571058531461 to 91.68391683916838,26.45034275546749 and SHA-256 227c9296079964ab3eff1b002200fd6a54925cec46b39ccaba91f1bd16801df2.
Its raw arc list is [[[-53,-40,-46,54]]], and decoded shared arcs meet kanauj, kamarupa and hindu-kingdoms.

The imported shape includes Karnasuvarna, much of Bengal, Pataliputra, Nalanda and northern Odisha but excludes Varanasi, Rohtasgarh, Ganjam, Kannauj, Prayagraj and Guwahati; it is a broad locator, not a surveyed reign boundary.
At 500 a broad Gupta Empire polygon owns all twenty audit points. At 700 the target vanishes and Palas prematurely own most eastern points; at 800 Palas remain widespread.
The chronology separates Shashanka's uncertain vassal phase, independent reign, secure 619 to 20 overlordship, death by the late 630s, successor fragmentation and only later Pala consolidation.

Daily-life claims distinguish direct Karnasuvarna archaeology, contemporary regional texts, later seventh-century continuity and broad period comparisons. No universal family, school, meal, outfit, cure, toilet or game is invented.

The written sample is an authentic Sanskrit clause from the 619 to 20 Ganjam charter, shown in normalized editorial Devanagari plus transliteration and translation; the copperplate itself uses transitional Gupta-to-Nagari lettering.
No appliesTo alias or forced direct successor is used; the atlas misspelling remains the exact card id while the card corrects it in prose.
